title: A pack's walling table
description: How a pack's builders laid walls of stone, by working (packs/<pack>/walling.json), read by the wall kind's plan stage as the table `walling` (kinds/wall.json; at R1, blender/generators/masonry.py through tools/r1_elevations.py) by the working a wall's, a rebuilt panel's or a stair's facts name. A working is a stone and the way it was laid: the course heights it was split or dressed to, its stones, copings, topstones, heads and through stones, its joints, its face's batter, its top's thickness and its copings' overhang, a rebuilt panel's edge stones, a stair's laps and joints. Every key a working's kind requires is required: the readers keep no defaults, so a missing key is an error. The wall's structure (its parapet, its stepped top, its heads' form, its panels' teeth) is the kind's, and the rules of any wall (level beds, SN10's bond, SN2's sliver and acute limits) are code's. Integers only, in millimetres, as every fact. tools/validate_record.py also checks what this schema cannot say: each range's least is no more than its most, each working's material is one of the pack's, and a test table's workings are not the pack's own.

applies.description: A test table's alone (design.md 7b, a style changed by data alone): the workings it sets a wall's facts to name, merged into a copy of the pack's table for the check. A pack's own table has none.

walls.description: The working the walls are laid in.

rebuilt.description: The working a rebuilt panel is relaid in.

workings.description: The workings, each under its name (a word; the facts name a working by it).

notes.description: Why each number is what it is, by working or by field name.

rangeMm.description: The least and the most, in millimetres.

fraction.description: A fraction: its numerator and its denominator.

anyOf.description: a rebuilt panel's: its edges are its own, and the line it is relaid to (its joints, batter, top and copings' overhang)

material.description: Its stone: materials/<material>.json in the pack, whose wear and cracking are the material's own.

mortar.description: What it was bedded in: none for a dry wall, or the mortar's name.

built.description: The year the builders laid it.

stock.description: Where its stones came from, where not new (reclaimed: the wall's own, relaid).

riseOneMm.description: A stair's rise up to this is one course; over it, one line between, the lower course the larger.

foundationMm.description: The foundation courses under the foot: larger than any rise.

drawnPerHeight.description: A face stone's drawn length, least and most, as fractions of its course's height (within stoneMm and SN10's 4.5).

shortMm.description: The least a stone may be where the geometry leaves a run no whole stones fill; flagged.

copeNominalMm.description: Its nominal thickness: the ideal bed is the pitch line plus the kind's parapet less this.

copeLeastMm.description: The least a coping slab may be where a level run or a panel leaves less than a whole one; flagged.

topstoneMm.description: A topstone's length at a wall's end (its form, square or not, is the kind's).

headTieMm.description: A head's tie, through the wall, as its face shows.

headRunnerMm.description: A head's runner along one face.

throughFirstMm.description: The first through stone from a panel's start.

throughEveryMm.description: And then one about this often.

jointMm.description: A joint's width between two of the wall's stones, its faces' and its copings' (a stone is set into its cell by half of one on each side). A stair's tread joints are steps.jointMm.

batterPerHeight.description: How far the face leans back for its height, back then up ([1, 6] is one in six, [0, 1] plumb). Only the face is cut at it; the beds stay level.

topThickMm.description: The wall's thickness at its top, under the coping.

copeOverMm.description: How much wider a standing wall's coping is than the wall's top: its overhangs on both faces together.

copeProudMm.description: How far a coping's front stands proud of the face under it, least and most; its back stands the rest of copeOverMm.

edgeStonesMm.description: A rebuilt panel's end stones against the old work: long, then short, in alternate courses.

steps.description: A stair's block steps laid in this working (SN3, SN5).

lapMm.description: A step's front bears this far on the back of the one below.

jointClearMm.description: No joint within this of the joint on the step below.
